sections.title: About Hisab
sections.body: Hisab is a shared expense, debt, and repayment tracker created by Hantalyze. This notice describes the information the app needs to run accounts, shared ledgers, and related support. Acknowledging this notice records that you have read it.

sections.title: Account and sign-in information
sections.body: When you register, Hisab collects your name, email address and password. The service stores a password hash, an internal account ID, a shareable Hisab ID, your registration date, and preferences such as your theme. Verification and password recovery use your registered inbox where eligible. Brevo delivers account emails. Recovery codes expire after 20 minutes, and the app server stores a digest to verify each code. A successful password reset revokes previous sessions.

sections.title: Profile pictures
sections.body: New profile pictures are cropped and saved privately on the device for the signed-in account. Choosing a photo does not automatically upload it. Photos uploaded by earlier versions can remain on the server and may be displayed when the account is shown to another user. A reset of the local picture changes its display on that device.

sections.title: Shared ledgers and invitations
sections.body: Hisab stores group names, membership and invitation records, and the amounts, descriptions, dates and people involved in ledger entries. Current group members can see the shared ledger, including entries that involve former members. Invitations identify the group and sender to the recipient. Your Hisab ID lets other users find your display name and invite you. Keep passwords, bank details and other unrelated private information out of descriptions and group names.

sections.title: Storage and service providers
sections.body: Hisab stores account information, group data, invitations, agreement records, and data requests in MongoDB Atlas. The service runs on Render and can store previously uploaded photos on a server volume. Android keeps a local copy of previously loaded records, theme settings, private photos, and encrypted sign-in details. GitHub distributes app updates and hosts the public support tracker. These providers process information needed for their respective services.

sections.title: Access and security
sections.body: Hisab uses authenticated requests, group membership checks, and administrator permissions to restrict access. Authorized administrators can see account information and manage account status. The service records administrative changes. Hisab uses HTTPS on its production service and stores password hashes. Keep your device and inbox secured and report concerns using a private channel.

sections.title: How long information is kept
sections.body: Deleting a Hisab removes it from your list and saves a private historical recovery source for up to two calendar months. Its expiry date is set when it is deleted; recovery does not extend it. Automatic database expiration removes the source and its archived records independently of app use. Recovery jobs normally deliver a read-only copy within 3-5 minutes while the service is running. A delivered recovered copy remains until you delete it or your account. Deleting a recovered copy permanently removes its recovery source and job; it cannot be recovered again. Shared active records remain accessible to other current members.

sections.title: Your data and privacy requests
sections.body: Settings, under Privacy and data, lets you select deleted Hisabs for recovery, view or permanently delete recovered read-only copies, and permanently delete your signed-in account after entering its password. Account deletion removes your sign-in information, private archives, copies, jobs, notification registrations and exclusively personal data. Financial records shared with other members are retained with your account identity anonymized. Personal files are queued for automatic cleanup. You can edit your profile normally. For other privacy questions or rights under applicable law, request a private support channel through About. GitHub issues are public.

sections.title: Children and changes to this notice
sections.body: Hisab is intended for people who can manage or participate in a shared expense ledger. If you believe a child’s information has been provided and needs attention, submit a privacy request or ask for a private support channel. The app shows the current version of this notice and asks you to acknowledge an updated version when its changes require it.
